chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) granted permission regarding al-'araya (date palm loans) that one may buy [the palm] for its measure of dates.

He said: 'And al-'araya is the plural of 'ariyyah, which is the palm tree that belongs to a man in the house of another man, so it is permissible for him to sell it for its measure of dates, and this permission does not apply to anything else.'

key_terms.الْعَرَايَا: Plural of 'ariyyah; date palm loans or lent palm trees
key_terms.خِرْصِهَا: Its measure or estimate (referring to the size/quantity of the palm)
key_terms.عَرِيَّةٍ: A lent item, specifically a date palm in this context

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling a lent date palm tree in exchange for dates?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific juristic exception of *al-'araya*, where a date palm lent to another is permitted to be sold for a fixed quantity of dates, distinguishing it from general loan contracts. Al-Skuni and the chain of narrators highlight that this permission is exclusive to date palms due to their unique agricultural nature, a nuance emphasized by Shia scholars to prevent ambiguity in commercial transactions.
